text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /private/tmp/donor-name-design-20261008/b/design.md
+# Candidate B: deterministic donor groups with scored audit
+
+## Problem
+
+Donor observations with the same usable normalized name must share an identity even when their addresses disagree or their Splink score is low. Existing Rust resolution consumes scored profile pairs, skips pairs of numbered companies, checks address disagreement before acceptance, and labels every merged unanchored component statistical. A separate deterministic grouping operation makes the new rule independent of model calibration. It must still produce an audited pair for every attempted donor merge and use the existing component constraints.
+
+Grounding: `input.rs::scoring_input` groups name/address profiles and adds repeat rows for real self-profile scoring. `model.json` blocks exact names when either profile needs resolution. `identity.rs::expanded_edges` expands scores and excludes pairs of anchored companies. `Components::new` seeds company-number groups; `apply` enforces pair and union constraints; `outcomes` emits identities. `ResolvedDeclarations::from_scored` calls identity resolution and computes attribution independently. No attribution changes belong in this design.
+
+## Usage
+
+The CLI and service still call the existing operation:
+
+```rust
+let result = ResolvedDeclarations::from_scored(&input, &scoring, scores, &run_key)?;
+```
+
+Two addressless Gary Lubner donors produce one local identity and `donor_name_link` outcomes. Their audit row retains the actual Splink probability and records `exact_donor_name`, including when the score is below 0.999.
+
+A donor and a payer sharing a name still require the old exact numbered-address and probability rule. If that link attaches a payer to a donor-name component, the output reports `mixed_link` when the complete component needs name-based connections. Donors carrying accepted company numbers continue to report `source_reported_company` for their own observations.
+
+The only internal entry remains `identity::resolve`. The caller does not coordinate grouping, scoring or component operations.
+
+## Shape
+
+Keep all new logic private in `identity.rs`. Make donor-name groups a source of eligible pair keys, independent of score classification. Scored candidates remain the single mutable audit map. Join donor pair keys to this map before mutating components; missing real scores are an error, never a probability of 1.0 or a fabricated comparison level.
+
+```rust
+type PairKey = (FunderObservationId, FunderObservationId); // ordered
+type CandidateEdges = BTreeMap<PairKey, PairDecision>;
+
+struct DonorNameGroups<'a> {
+    members: BTreeMap<&'a str, Vec<&'a FunderObservationId>>,
+}
+
+impl<'a> DonorNameGroups<'a> {
+    /// Donor role only; nonempty checked normalized name; no address filter.
+    fn from_input(input: &'a ResolutionInput) -> Self { todo!() }
+    /// Every unordered observation pair, including company/company pairs.
+    /// Refuses the configured audit budget before materializing huge groups.
+    fn pairs(&self, budget: usize) -> Result<BTreeSet<PairKey>, EntityIngestionError> {
+        todo!()
+    }
+}
+
+enum LinkRule { DonorName, Statistical }
+
+/// Covers the whole donor-name group before any merge, so a name-only
+/// observation cannot attach arbitrarily to one of two company anchors.
+fn competing_anchors(
+    input: &ResolutionInput,
+    edges: &CandidateEdges,
+    donor_pairs: &BTreeSet<PairKey>,
+) -> BTreeSet<FunderObservationId> { todo!() }
+
+impl Components {
+    /// One owner for union state. Both rules share type/anchor constraints.
+    fn apply(
+        &mut self,
+        input: &ResolutionInput,
+        edges: &mut CandidateEdges,
+        donor_pairs: &BTreeSet<PairKey>,
+    ) { todo!() }
+
+    /// Derives component evidence from accepted audit rows after unions finish.
+    fn outcomes(
+        &self,
+        input: &ResolutionInput,
+        edges: &CandidateEdges,
+        run_key: &str,
+    ) -> Vec<ObservationResolution> { todo!() }
+}
+```
+
+`PairReason::ExactDonorName` records acceptance by the new deterministic policy. `probability`, `name_level`, and `address_level` keep their worker values. Do not add optional scores or a second deterministic audit format. The boundary must provide real scores for the full required donor pair set.
+
+To guarantee that coverage, `scoring_input` marks every profile containing a donor as `needs_resolution`, even when all its observations have company numbers. It also adds a repeat row for repeated profiles containing donors. Existing exact-name blocking then covers every donor-name pair. Expansion keeps donor/donor company pairs while retaining the exclusion for other fully anchored pairs. Before resolution, compare deterministic donor keys with expanded scored keys and refuse incomplete coverage. This is a checked completeness boundary, per boundary-discipline. Profile count and expanded audit count obey the existing budget.
+
+`apply` first computes eligible links. Donor keys select `DonorName` before address checks. Other candidates keep the old `strong` predicate and full-address rejection. Explicit person/organisation conflicts apply to both. Competing-anchor detection examines every eligible link before unions. Apply donor-name links first in ordered pair order, then statistical links, through the same component union operation. A component union may not combine distinct company numbers or explicit person/organisation kinds.
+
+Company ambiguity needs group-wide handling. For an exact donor-name group containing distinct company anchors, unanchored members remain review candidates against every anchored member. They may merge with other unanchored compatible donors, but may not inherit whichever anchor happens to sort first. Same-number anchors remain seeded together. A donor pair spanning different anchors is rejected by the union invariant. Unknown-kind observations cannot bridge explicit person and organisation components.
+
+Add `IdentityBasis::DonorNameLink` and `IdentityBasis::MixedLink`. Derive evidence after final components, per single-source-of-truth. Build a support partition using company-number seeds and every accepted edge satisfying the original `strong` predicate, including donor-name accepted edges whose genuine score and address happen to satisfy it. For each final component:
+
+- If statistical/address support connects the entire component, report `statistical_link` for non-source observations.
+- If name-based membership is necessary and there is no statistical/address link within it, report `donor_name_link`.
+- If name-based membership is necessary and statistical/address links support part of it, report `mixed_link`.
+
+Source-number observations override the component label with `source_reported_company`. Singleton and unresolved outcomes retain current behavior. This definition describes support for the complete assigned identity, so a strong pair inside a larger name-only component cannot claim the whole identity is statistically established. Redundant weak edges do not downgrade a fully supported component. The support partition is derived inside `outcomes`, not maintained alongside mutable union state.
+
+The public interface remains one operation. Internally the added grouping map hides name enumeration and completeness checking. Component state still has one writer. Types separate eligible rule from scored evidence instead of letting a float imply eligibility, per model-the-domain.
+
+## Synthesis decision
+
+Candidate B proposes separate donor-name grouping as the base. The orchestrator fills the final synthesis decision after comparison.
+
+## Tradeoffs accepted
+
+- We accept a second private pair-key set and a completeness check in exchange for proving donor membership does not depend on scorer calibration or accidental candidate omissions.
+- We accept real scoring work for anchored donor profiles in exchange for complete uniform audit rows and unchanged probability fields.
+- We accept quadratic pair audits within repeated names in exchange for inspecting every possible donor-name pair. The existing explicit budget remains a refusal boundary.
+- We accept component-wide mixed labels in exchange for a precise claim about the complete identity; accepted pair rows retain local support detail.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+1. Integrate exact donor matching directly into scored-edge classification. This has the smaller implementation: `eligible_rule(input, edge)` returns `Option<LinkRule>`, and no separate pair set or grouping pass is needed. The unchanged exact-name blocking already covers most donors. It loses the direct completeness proof unless the boundary adds an explicit candidate-coverage invariant. This is a strong alternative if implementation size is the primary deciding factor; retain the support partition and anchored-profile coverage fixes from this candidate.
+2. Seed equal names directly in `Components::new`, like company numbers. This appears smaller but bypasses pair dispositions and allows incompatible kinds or competing anchors into initial components. Repairing that requires a second checked grouping algorithm and a second audit construction path. Reject it.
+3. Add unscored deterministic audit rows with optional probabilities. This removes the scoring dependency but expands the output contract and duplicates pair creation. It also forces every downstream consumer to understand scored and unscored cases. Reject it for this task.
+
+## Implementation reconciliation
+
+No implementation or accepted deviations yet. All repository source was read only.
+
+## Open questions and risks
+
+Can candidate expansion and profile coverage expose a repeated-name group larger than the current configured budget? The required behavior is refusal with the existing explicit budget instruction, never partial grouping. No user decision is required.
+
+Does the implementation preserve company ambiguity across donor-name groups that acquire anchors through old statistical links? The pre-merge ambiguity pass must consider the eligible graph rather than donor groups in isolation. A component with routes to two anchors must not select one by iteration order. This deserves a regression fixture.
+
+## Next implementation step
+
+First add fixtures for low-score donor pairs, disagreeing addresses, complete repeated-profile audit, competing anchors through mixed links, and component evidence; then implement the grouped candidate coverage and shared union policy, bump the policy version, and update resolution docs.
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
Created [candidate B design](/private/tmp/donor-name-design-20261008/b/design.md).

It separates deterministic donor grouping from scores, joins every donor pair to genuine scored audit evidence, and derives honest component-wide name/statistical/mixed identity bases. It compares the smaller scored-edge integration alternative and identifies anchored-profile coverage and competing-anchor safeguards. Source remains unchanged.
